title: Batch/cmd launcher invokes a workspace script without forwarding -WorkspacePath
description: Windows Terminal / cmd launchers (Launch-*.bat) that invoke workspace PowerShell scripts via -File <root>\scripts\X.ps1 must forward -WorkspacePath so the child resolves the same workspace root. Omitting it makes scripts fall back to a guessed root (Split-Path $PSScriptRoot -Parent), which diverges when launched from a different working directory and breaks config/report/log path resolution. Encountered while repairing Launch-ServiceClusterTabs.bat tabs.
detection_method: Regex scan (batch/cmd only) for a -File invocation of a scripts\*.ps1 path that has no -WorkspacePath argument on the same line. A negative lookahead excludes known launcher utilities that intentionally do not accept -WorkspacePath (they self-resolve their root), keeping the pattern free of false positives.
false_positive_note: Launcher scripts without a -WorkspacePath parameter are excluded via negative lookahead: Scan-WorkspaceVersions.ps1, Start-Engines.ps1, Show-ScanDashboard.ps1, Show-EventLogViewer.ps1, Show-MCPServiceConfig.ps1 (verified param-less 2026-06-18). Add new param-less launchers here rather than forcing -WorkspacePath onto a script that cannot bind it.
preventionRule: Every batch/cmd invocation of a workspace script that accepts -WorkspacePath must pass -WorkspacePath %WS% (or the resolved root).
remedy:
REM BEFORE
pwsh -NoProfile -File %WS%\scripts\Invoke-Foo.ps1
REM AFTER
pwsh -NoProfile -File %WS%\scripts\Invoke-Foo.ps1 -WorkspacePath %WS%
